metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ecuador strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
Hey David, I was thinking we should get some flowers for Tom's celebration. What do you think about carnations? 

I’m not sure... Carnations? Aren't there better options? Maybe something more special... 

I get that, but carnations are classic and signify admiration. They could really show our support. 

Support... hmm. I just think flowers don't really convey what I feel... But do you really think they’ll make a difference? 

Absolutely! They’re a small gesture that can mean a lot. Besides, it’s a way to celebrate his achievement. 

I suppose... But what about the idea of making our parents proud? Do you think that's a main goal in life?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message:
I definitely think making our parents proud is important. For me, it's one of my main goals in life. Growing up in Ecuador, family values really shape our perspectives. It's about honoring their sacrifices and showing them that their support mattered. 

But back to Tom—do you think something like a nice bottle of wine might be more fitting instead of flowers?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: I get your perspective, but I don't think making our parents proud should be a *main* goal in life. It feels limiting. As for Tom, a nice bottle of wine could be good, but it still feels a bit... typical, you know? Wouldn't flowers be more memorable?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, but for me, making my parents proud isn't limiting; it's motivating. It's about building a legacy and showing gratitude for what they’ve done. I do think flowers can be memorable, especially if we choose the right type. But if you feel strongly about wine, maybe we can combine both? A thoughtful card with the flowers could add a personal touch. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: I see your point, but I still disagree on making parents proud being a main goal. It feels like it takes away from individual aspirations. Combining both... that could work. A card with the flowers might add a personal touch, yes. I just want to make sure it feels *right* for Tom.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I get that, but for me, making my parents proud is an essential part of who I am. It drives me to achieve my aspirations while keeping family values close. I think Tom would appreciate the flowers and the card. It shows we care about his achievement and honor what he represents in his career. Let's go with that; I feel it reflects our support well. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: That's... definitely a strong sentiment. I respect that it drives you. I can agree that Tom would appreciate the flowers and the card. It does show support and honor his achievement. So, if we go with that, I’m okay. It just feels important to get it right.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I don’t really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it’s all the same; we all want to support Tom in our own ways. People figure it out as they go along. Whether it’s about making our parents proud or pursuing individual aspirations, what matters is the gesture behind it. So, if we go with the flowers and the card, it feels like the right way to go for Tom’s celebration. What do you say we get those arranged?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I suppose you have a point about the gesture. It does matter. If flowers and a card are what you feel is right, then let's arrange that. It’s about supporting Tom in a way that resonates with us. So... flowers and card it is.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message:
Great! I’m glad we could agree on that. Flowers and a card will definitely convey our support for Tom’s achievement. It feels meaningful, and I think he will appreciate it. Thank you for being open to this. Let’s make it special for him! 

GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Acceptance
